item.title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
item.description:
Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open.
The flaw,&nbsp;CVE-2026-112900, is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript, a separate program it runs to turn the image into pixels, without checking the name first.
item.dc:creator: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)

item.description:

item.title: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
item.description:
Right now, there is probably an AI agent running on a laptop somewhere in your network. It stores API keys and database passwords, can access your internal systems, and works without anyone watching.
Nobody reviewed its access. Nobody owns it.
If an employee had that much reach with that little oversight, you would call it an insider risk. So why do we still call the agent a productivity tool?

OpenAI has revealed that two artificial intelligence (AI) agents powered by GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra weakened misalignment monitoring while making requested software changes during two internal coding tasks.

item.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
item.description: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

item.title: PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts Emerge
item.description:
PHP has released emergency updates that fix two critical flaws in the language itself, letting an attacker without an account run code on a web server. The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the PHP team says only updating fully protects a server.

item.title: Google Chrome Adds ClickFix Warnings to Stop Users From Running Malicious Commands
item.description:
Google on Tuesday said it's rolling out improved safeguards in its Chrome browser to secure users against ClickFix attacks when Enhanced Protection is enabled.
ClickFix is a popular social engineering technique in which bad actors trick users into copying and pasting malicious code directly into their computer's operating system, thereby bypassing conventional security controls.
